title: Man City found guilty of majority of 115 financial rule breaches
description: The club, which denies all wrongdoing, is accused of breaching the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

title: Relegation? Titles stripped? Appeals? What next for Man City
description: It has taken more than two years, but a judgement finally appears to have been made on the financial rule breaches levelled against the club. Here's what it means.

title: Iran offers US deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days
description: Asked about the Iranian offer, a US official told the BBC "constructive discussions" were taking place through mediators.

title: E-bikes seized by police sold on at auction, BBC finds
description: Thousands are confiscated annually because they are suspected of being driven illegally or used in a crime - most are destroyed, but last year police sold at least 161.

title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach
description: Current and former agents speak to the BBC about the devastating impact of the FBI hack.

title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites
description: OpenAI said its bots accessed public data from the US Census and the Securities and Exchange Commission, which regulates US stock markets.

title: I'm not tempted to call an early election, Burnham says
description: The prime minister told the BBC an early poll would throw the country into a "backward-looking process".

title: Black woman found hanging from tree was dead before body was 'staged', police say
description: Tasia Fortune's body was found hanging from a tree on the grounds of an abandoned home in Jackson in August.

title: South African white genocide does not exist, new ambassador to US tells BBC
description: Roelf Meyer tells the BBC that being a white Afrikaner gives him legitimacy to challenge Trump's claim of a genocide.
